entryPoint: Dept::isActive() in include/class.dept.php (lines 179-181): a zero-argument public instance method returning `!!($this->flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE)`.
coreLogic: The entire logic is one inline expression: bitwise AND of the packed `flags` int against the class constant FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0004), coerced to a strict PHP boolean via the double-negation `!!` idiom. Dept packs six independent flag bits into the single `flags` column (class.dept.php:73-78): FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY (0x0001), FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM (0x0002), FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0004), FLAG_ARCHIVED (0x0008), FLAG_ASSIGN_PRIMARY_ONLY (0x0010), FLAG_DISABLE_REOPEN_AUTO_ASSIGN (0x0020) — isActive() only ever inspects the FLAG_ACTIVE bit and is indifferent to all others, including FLAG_ARCHIVED. Related but out-of-chain methods that independently touch the same bit and must not be altered: getStatus() (lines 166-173, bare `&` tri-state 'Active'/'Archived'/'Disabled' string, does not call isActive()); allowsReopen() (lines 175-177, checks FLAG_ARCHIVED only); hasFlag($flag) (lines 597-599, a generic bit-test helper reading via $this->get('flags',0) — isActive() does not call it and it does not call isActive()); setFlag($flag,$val) (lines 589-595, the sole mutator of flags, invoked from Dept::update()'s status-switch at lines 886-899 — writes flags but is never read by isActive()); the static ORM filter criterion `'flags__hasbit' => Dept::FLAG_ACTIVE` used for 'activeonly' queries (line 665); and the bulk-list loop `$row['flags'] & self::FLAG_ACTIVE` inside getDepartments() (lines 680-686), which recomputes the same bit directly off raw query rows without ever instantiating isActive().

inputShape: None. isActive() takes zero parameters. Its sole implicit input is $this->flags (int), the packed bitmask column already present in memory on the Dept instance as loaded by the ORM (VerySimpleModel) — isActive() performs no lazy-load, no fetch, and reads nothing else.
outputShape: A strict PHP boolean produced by double-negating (`!!`) the bitwise-AND of $this->flags against Dept::FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0004): true when the FLAG_ACTIVE bit is set (regardless of whether FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY, FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM, FLAG_ARCHIVED, FLAG_ASSIGN_PRIMARY_ONLY, or FLAG_DISABLE_REOPEN_AUTO_ASSIGN bits are also set), false when it is not set — including when flags is 0.
sideEffects: None inside isActive() itself: no DB reads or writes, no global state ($cfg or otherwise) read or written, no lazy-loading or caching triggered, no file I/O, and no mutation of $this or of any parameter (there are none) — it is a pure in-memory read of an already-populated scalar.

Context only (occurs before isActive() is invoked, not inside it): consumers obtain the Dept instance via Dept::lookup() (a DB SELECT, short-circuited by ModelInstanceManager's in-process cache for primary-key lookups per include/class.orm.php:590-610) or via an already-loaded ORM join/accessor (Staff::getDept() returning $this->dept, Topic::getDept() calling Dept::lookup() internally, Dept::getParent() calling static::lookup($this->ht['pid'])). None of this DB access happens as part of isActive() executing.
constraints: Preserve the bitwise `&` operator and the FLAG_ACTIVE = 0x0004 mask exactly; do not substitute logical `&&`, a different bit, or a different flags column.

Preserve the `!!` double-negation so the return value is a strict PHP boolean (true/false), not a truthy/falsy int, to keep byte-for-byte caller-visible behavior for both loose and strict comparisons.
Dept::isActive()'s method signature (zero args, public instance method) must remain unchanged on the facade after the strangler patch.

The extracted service must accept the raw `flags` int (or equivalent primitive) as a plain parameter, not the Dept object, and must never call back into Dept::isActive() or any other Dept instance method (anti-recursion).

Must not alter the independent, out-of-chain flag reads in Dept::getStatus(), Dept::allowsReopen(), Dept::hasFlag(), the `flags__hasbit` ORM filter, or the getDepartments() bulk-list loop — those are separate, pre-existing bitwise checks on the same or adjacent bits and are out of scope for this facade patch.

flags values with FLAG_ACTIVE unset but other bits set (e.g. FLAG_ARCHIVED alone, or FLAG_ARCHIVED combined with FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY/FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM/etc.) must continue to return false; flags with FLAG_ACTIVE set combined with any other bit(s) — including FLAG_ARCHIVED simultaneously set — must continue to return true, since the method is indifferent to every bit except FLAG_ACTIVE.

Do not touch include/class.sla.php, include/class.team.php, include/class.topic.php, or include/class.ticket.php — Topic::isActive() (sibling MOD-31 seam), SLA::isActive(), Team::isActive(), and Ticket's own dept-resolution call site at class.ticket.php:4260 are consumers to document only, not to edit.

This ticket's facade patch, extracted service, harness, fixtures, manifest, branch, and PR must remain fully independent of any other concurrent MOD ticket's artifacts (e.g. MOD-31's TopicActiveChecker, MOD-25's SLA grace-period work).
harnessInputShape: JSON input has a single field: flags (int) — the raw Dept bitmask value to set directly on an in-memory Dept object's `flags` property (without saving to the DB, since isActive() only reads the in-process property and has no other side effects to capture) before calling isActive() and recording the boolean return value. Use flags=4 for the 'active' fixture (FLAG_ACTIVE alone); flags=0 or flags=1/2 (other bits with FLAG_ACTIVE absent) for 'inactive'; flags=8 (FLAG_ARCHIVED alone, FLAG_ACTIVE bit absent) for 'archived-only'; and flags=12 (FLAG_ACTIVE|FLAG_ARCHIVED) or flags=23 (FLAG_ACTIVE combined with several other bits) for 'active-plus-other-flags', which must still return true since only the FLAG_ACTIVE bit is inspected.
